overview.body:
**Asanga** ​(*asanga*) ‌— ‌Yogacara, Mind-Only ​· ​Without ​attachment ​— ​belongs to ‌the ​Buddhist ​tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued ​under ‌the ​domain ​"Yogacara, Mind-Only". ​The ​name ​means ‌"Without ​attachment".

**Asanga** ‌is ​yogacara, ‌mind-only. ​The ‌name means ​"Without ‌attachment" ​and ​belongs ‌to ‌the buddhist ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex ​restores ‌the ​name as ​**Asanga** ‌and ​serves ​its ‌temple at ​[its ‌temple](https://punicodex.com/asanga/). ​The ​restoration ​needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ‌or ​diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form ​would ‌lose, ‌which ‌places ‌the name ​in ‌Tier ​2. ​The ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*asanga* ​survives ​as ‌a modern ​convenience ​imposed ​by ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system; ​the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the fallback, ‌is ​the ​form ​the ​project defends ‌as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name ‌is attested ‌in ​Devanagari ​as **असन्ग**. ​Etymologically ​it ​means "Without ‌attachment".

​The ​ASCII form ‌*asanga* ​survives ‌only ​because the ‌early ​domain-name ​system could ​not ​carry ​diacritics; it ‌is ​a ‌technological compromise, ​not ‌an ​ancient ‌spelling. The ​Unicode ‌restoration ​**Asanga** recovers ​the ‌full ‌diacritic detail ‌of ​the ​scholarly transliteration ‌directly ​in ​the ‌address bar. ​The ​restoration ‌needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ​or diacritics ​its ​ASCII ​form ‌would lose, ‌which ​places ‌the name ​in ​Tier ‌2.

The ‌letter-by-letter ‌transformation ‌runs:

- ​**a** ‌→ ​**A** ​— Same, ​capitalized
‌- ​**s** → ​**s** ​— ‌Same
- ​**a** ​→ ​**a** — ‌Same
​- ‌**n** ​→ **n** ‌— ​Same
‌- **g** ‌→ ​**g** ​— Same
​- ​**a** ‌→ **a** ‌— ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/asanga/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**asanga** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Asanga.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"asanga" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Asanga".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"asanga" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Asanga" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Asanga was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Asanga ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Asanga ‌place ​yogacara, mind-only ​at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living ​mythological world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Asanga ‌appears ​in buddhist ‌tradition ​as ​yogacara, mind-only. ​The ​name's ​meaning, "Without ‌attachment", ​shapes the ‌narratives ​told ‌about this ​figure.

‌### ​Worship and ‌Memory ​(Cult)

​Devotees and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ‌Asanga ​in ​ritual, text, ‌and ​iconography, ​ensuring the ‌name ​survived ​into the ‌modern ​scholarly record.

‌The ​myths ​of Asanga ​survive ​in ‌fragments, summaries, ‌and ​later ‌retellings. Each ​version ​reflects the ‌interests ‌of ‌its tellers ‌— ​poets, ‌priests, philosophers, ​and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does not ​privilege ​a ‌single version; ​it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. The ​restoration ‌Asanga ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Asanga ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Buddhist ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌असन्ग, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​yogacara ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Asanga ‌is to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of ​yogacara, Mind-Only ‌in ​the ​mind ‌and ​to ask ‌what ​of ‌it ​endures. ​The name ​means ​"Without ​attachment" ‌— ​and a ‌name ​that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning so ​openly ‌invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere recollection. ‌The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​yogacara, ‌Mind-Only ​· ​Without ‌attachment.

Sit ​with ‌the ​restored ​form ​— Asanga ​— ‌and ‌the ​diacritics ‌themselves become ​the ​practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ‌a small ​act ‌of ​attention, ​a ​refusal to ‌let ​the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form *asanga* ​stand ​in ​for ‌the ​whole. What ‌the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this name, ‌the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader to ‌preserve ‌in ​turn.
